# MCP tools reference

The BYOMailer MCP server has 45 tools. This page lists them in the order that `tools/list` returns them.

A script makes this page from the tool classes in `app/Mcp/Tools`. Each description is the text that the server sends to the agent.

The hint columns show the MCP tool annotations. A client can use them to ask a person before a call. A dash means that the tool does not set the hint.

Read [the MCP overview](overview.md) for the workflow and the error format.

## list-newsletters-tool

**List Newsletters Tool**

> List the newsletters belonging to the authenticated account, returning each id, title, status, subject and sent date. Use the returned id with the newsletter-stats-tool or newsletter-content-tool tools.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | string | No | `draft`, `scheduled`, `queued`, `ab_testing`, `sent`, `failed` | Optional status filter. |
| `search` | string | No |  | Optional case-insensitive search against the newsletter title and subject. |
| `limit` | integer | No |  | Maximum number of newsletters to return (1-100, default 25). |

## newsletter-stats-tool

**Newsletter Stats Tool**

> Get the delivery and engagement stats for a single newsletter: totals plus sent, delivered, opened, bounced, unsubscribed and complained counts with delivery/open/unsubscribe rates. Includes A/B variant metrics when A/B testing is enabled. Find the newsletter id with the list-newsletters-tool tool.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `newsletter_id` | integer | Yes |  | The id of the newsletter to read stats for. |

## link-clicks-tool

**Link Clicks Tool**

> Report who clicked which link in one newsletter or one sequence step. Without "link", it lists each link with its unique contacts, total clicks and click rate (unique contacts / delivered * 100). A named link (data-bm-link attribute) groups by its name. Any other link groups by its URL without utm_* parameters. With "link" set to a key from that list, it lists the contacts who clicked that link, page by page with after_id. Clicks can include link scanners, for example Microsoft Safe Links.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `newsletter_id` | integer | No |  | The newsletter to report on. Send this or sequence_id with step_id. |
| `sequence_id` | integer | No |  | The sequence of the step. Required with step_id. |
| `step_id` | integer | No |  | The sequence step to report on. |
| `link` | string | No |  | A link key from the link list ("name:<link name>" or "url:<url>"). When set, the tool lists the contacts who clicked that link. |
| `limit` | integer | No |  | Contacts per page when "link" is set. Default 50, maximum 200. |
| `after_id` | integer | No |  | The next_after_id of the previous page. |

## newsletter-content-tool

**Newsletter Content Tool**

> Get the full content of a single newsletter: title, subject, preview text, sender, html and text body, content variables (the saved default of each {{ variable }}), detected variables (the {{ variables }} that the content uses), and the B variant content when A/B testing is enabled. Find the newsletter id with the list-newsletters-tool tool.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `newsletter_id` | integer | Yes |  | The id of the newsletter to read content for. |

## view-newsletter-filters-tool

**View Newsletter Filters Tool**

> Describe the audience targeting filters available when creating a newsletter for the authenticated account. Returns the filter schema (categories, operators, modes) plus the account's concrete building blocks: tags, lists, topics, attribute keys, countries, timezones and newsletters that can be referenced by id/name in a filter. Use the result to assemble the "filters" array for the calculate-newsletter-contacts-tool and create-newsletter-tool tools.

This tool takes no arguments.

## calculate-newsletter-contacts-tool

**Calculate Newsletter Contacts Tool**

> Count how many contacts would receive a newsletter sent to the given audience filters, without creating or sending anything. Pass the same "filters" array you would use with create-newsletter-tool (omit it to count every active contact). Use view-newsletter-filters-tool to discover valid filter values. Returns the recipient count and the sanitized filters that were applied.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filters` | array of object | No |  | Audience targeting filters. Omit to target every active contact. |
| `filters[].connector` | string | No | `and`, `or` | How this filter joins the previous one. Defaults to "and". |
| `filters[].category` | string | No | `attributes`, `tags`, `lists`, `topics`, `date`, `engagement`, `location` | The filter category. |
| `filters[].mode` | string | No | `all`, `any`, `none` | Match mode for attributes/tags/lists/topics (location uses any\|none). |
| `filters[].operator` | string | No |  | Operator for date or engagement filters. |
| `filters[].field` | string | No |  | Field for location filters: country or timezone. |
| `filters[].values` | array | No |  | Filter values. Shape depends on category — see view-newsletter-filters-tool. |

## create-newsletter-tool

**Create Newsletter Tool**

> Create a draft newsletter for the authenticated account. Drafts are never sent. Schedule a draft with schedule-newsletter after the user confirms. Optionally attach a sender (email_identity_id), template (email_template_id), audience filters and content_variables (the default value of each {{ variable }}). Use view-newsletter-filters-tool to build the filters array and calculate-newsletter-contacts-tool to preview the audience size first. Returns the new newsletter id and status.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | No |  | Internal title for the newsletter. Defaults to "Untitled newsletter". |
| `subject` | string | No |  | Email subject line. Supports {{ variable }} template tags. |
| `preview_text` | string | No |  | Inbox preview / preheader text. |
| `html_content` | string | No |  | HTML body of the email. Plain-text is derived automatically. |
| `email_identity_id` | integer | No |  | Verified sender identity id to send from. Required before the draft can be scheduled or test-mailed. |
| `email_template_id` | integer | No |  | Optional email template id to wrap the content. |
| `filters` | array of object | No |  | Audience targeting filters. Omit to target every active contact. |
| `filters[].connector` | string | No | `and`, `or` | How this filter joins the previous one. Defaults to "and". |
| `filters[].category` | string | No | `attributes`, `tags`, `lists`, `topics`, `date`, `engagement`, `location` | The filter category. |
| `filters[].mode` | string | No | `all`, `any`, `none` | Match mode for attributes/tags/lists/topics (location uses any\|none). |
| `filters[].operator` | string | No |  | Operator for date or engagement filters. |
| `filters[].field` | string | No |  | Field for location filters: country or timezone. |
| `filters[].values` | array | No |  | Filter values. Shape depends on category — see view-newsletter-filters-tool. |
| `content_variables` | object | No |  | Default values of the {{ variable }} placeholders, as an object of variable name to text (maximum 255 characters each). A default fills the placeholder when the contact has no value for it, for example {"checkout_url": "https://example.com/checkout"}. The object replaces all saved defaults. An empty object clears them. |

## update-newsletter-tool

**Update Newsletter Tool**

> Update a draft or scheduled newsletter for the authenticated account. A scheduled newsletter is live: it sends to real contacts at its scheduled time, so the tool refuses the change until you ask the user to confirm and call it again with confirm_live set to true. A newsletter that is sending or already sent is locked and this tool returns an error. The status never changes here: use schedule-newsletter to schedule or unschedule. Pass content_variables to replace the default value of each {{ variable }}. Only the fields you pass are changed; omitted fields keep their current values. Use view-newsletter-filters-tool to build the filters array and calculate-newsletter-contacts-tool to preview the audience size first. Returns the newsletter id and status.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `newsletter_id` | integer | Yes |  | Id of the draft or scheduled newsletter to update. Use list-newsletters-tool to discover ids. |
| `title` | string | No |  | Internal title for the newsletter. |
| `subject` | string | No |  | Email subject line. Supports {{ variable }} template tags. |
| `preview_text` | string | No |  | Inbox preview / preheader text. |
| `html_content` | string | No |  | HTML body of the email. Plain-text is derived automatically. |
| `email_identity_id` | integer | No |  | Verified sender identity id to send from. Required before the draft can be scheduled or test-mailed. |
| `email_template_id` | integer | No |  | Optional email template id to wrap the content. |
| `filters` | array of object | No |  | Audience targeting filters. Omit to target every active contact. |
| `filters[].connector` | string | No | `and`, `or` | How this filter joins the previous one. Defaults to "and". |
| `filters[].category` | string | No | `attributes`, `tags`, `lists`, `topics`, `date`, `engagement`, `location` | The filter category. |
| `filters[].mode` | string | No | `all`, `any`, `none` | Match mode for attributes/tags/lists/topics (location uses any\|none). |
| `filters[].operator` | string | No |  | Operator for date or engagement filters. |
| `filters[].field` | string | No |  | Field for location filters: country or timezone. |
| `filters[].values` | array | No |  | Filter values. Shape depends on category — see view-newsletter-filters-tool. |
| `content_variables` | object | No |  | Default values of the {{ variable }} placeholders, as an object of variable name to text (maximum 255 characters each). A default fills the placeholder when the contact has no value for it, for example {"checkout_url": "https://example.com/checkout"}. The object replaces all saved defaults. An empty object clears them. |
| `confirm_live` | boolean | No |  | Set to true only after the user explicitly confirms the change to a live record. A live record affects real contacts now. Leave it out for drafts. |

## send-newsletter-test-mail-tool

**Send Newsletter Test Mail Tool**

> Send a one-off test copy of a newsletter to the authenticated user's own email address so they can preview it. The newsletter must already have a sender identity attached. Does not send to the newsletter audience. Find the newsletter id with list-newsletters-tool or create-newsletter-tool.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `newsletter_id` | integer | Yes |  | The id of the newsletter to send a test copy of. |

## schedule-newsletter

**Schedule Newsletter Tool**

> Schedule a draft newsletter to send at a future time (action "schedule"), move a scheduled newsletter to a new time (action "schedule"), or cancel the schedule and return it to draft (action "unschedule"). This affects real contacts, so the first call only returns a preview: the change, the send time and the number of recipients. Nothing is saved. Show the preview to the user, and after the user confirms, call the tool again with the same arguments and confirm_live set to true. Never set confirm_live without that confirmation. The dashboard runs the same checks before scheduling: subject and body, the SES account status, and the SES permissions. A missing {{ unsubscribe_url }} link or a missing postal address never blocks the schedule. The preview and the result list them in warnings. Show the warnings to the user. Set the sender first with update-newsletter-tool. This tool never sends a newsletter immediately.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `newsletter_id` | integer | Yes |  | Id of the newsletter. Use list-newsletters-tool to discover ids. |
| `action` | string | Yes | `schedule`, `unschedule` | "schedule" sets or moves the send time. "unschedule" returns a scheduled newsletter to draft. |
| `scheduled_at` | string | No |  | Required for "schedule". The send time in ISO 8601 with a UTC offset, for example 2026-11-02T09:00:00-05:00. It must be in the future. |
| `confirm_live` | boolean | No |  | Set to true only after the user explicitly confirms the change to a live record. A live record affects real contacts now. Leave it out for drafts. |

**List Sequences Tool**

> List the sequences belonging to the authenticated account, returning each id, name, status, step count and contact count. Use the returned id with the sequence-stats-tool or sequence-content-tool tools.

| `limit` | integer | No |  | Maximum number of sequences to return (1-100, default 25). |

## create-sequence-tool

**Create Sequence Tool**

> Create a draft sequence (automated drip campaign) for the authenticated account. Sequences are always created as drafts. Activate a sequence with set-sequence-status after the user confirms. Pass filters to limit which contacts the sequence targets (use view-newsletter-filters-tool to build them). Pass content_variables to set the default value of each {{ variable }} that the steps use, for example a fallback checkout_url. Add steps with create-sequence-step-tool and edit the sequence later with update-sequence-tool. Returns the new sequence id, status, saved filters and content variables.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes |  | Name for the sequence. |
| `filters` | array of object | No |  | Sequence filters. Only contacts who match them receive the sequence. Use view-newsletter-filters-tool to build the array. Omit to target every active contact. |
| `filters[].connector` | string | No | `and`, `or` | How this filter joins the previous one. Defaults to "and". |
| `filters[].category` | string | No | `attributes`, `tags`, `lists`, `topics`, `date`, `engagement`, `location` | The filter category. |
| `filters[].mode` | string | No | `all`, `any`, `none` | Match mode for attributes/tags/lists/topics (location uses any\|none). |
| `filters[].operator` | string | No |  | Operator for date or engagement filters. |
| `filters[].field` | string | No |  | Field for location filters: country or timezone. |
| `filters[].values` | array | No |  | Filter values. Shape depends on category — see view-newsletter-filters-tool. |
| `content_variables` | object | No |  | Default values of the {{ variable }} placeholders, as an object of variable name to text (maximum 255 characters each). A default fills the placeholder when the contact has no value for it, for example {"checkout_url": "https://example.com/checkout"}. The object replaces all saved defaults. An empty object clears them. |

## update-sequence-tool

**Update Sequence Tool**

> Update a sequence of any status. A live sequence sends to real contacts now, so the tool refuses the change until you ask the user to confirm and call it again with confirm_live set to true. Draft and paused sequences need no confirmation. The status never changes here: use set-sequence-status. Only the fields you pass are changed; omitted fields keep their current values. Pass filters to replace the sequence filters (an empty array clears them). Filters and a saved segment are exclusive, so passing filters removes a saved segment from the sequence. Pass content_variables to replace the default values of the {{ variables }} (an empty object clears them). Find sequence ids with list-sequences-tool and read the current filters and content variables with sequence-content-tool. Returns the sequence id, status, saved filters and content variables.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sequence_id` | integer | Yes |  | Id of the sequence to update. Use list-sequences-tool to discover sequence ids. |
| `name` | string | No |  | New name for the sequence. |
| `filters` | array of object | No |  | Sequence filters. Only contacts who match them receive the sequence. Use view-newsletter-filters-tool to build the array. The array replaces the current filters. Pass an empty array to clear them. |
| `filters[].connector` | string | No | `and`, `or` | How this filter joins the previous one. Defaults to "and". |
| `filters[].category` | string | No | `attributes`, `tags`, `lists`, `topics`, `date`, `engagement`, `location` | The filter category. |
| `filters[].mode` | string | No | `all`, `any`, `none` | Match mode for attributes/tags/lists/topics (location uses any\|none). |
| `filters[].operator` | string | No |  | Operator for date or engagement filters. |
| `filters[].field` | string | No |  | Field for location filters: country or timezone. |
| `filters[].values` | array | No |  | Filter values. Shape depends on category — see view-newsletter-filters-tool. |
| `content_variables` | object | No |  | Default values of the {{ variable }} placeholders, as an object of variable name to text (maximum 255 characters each). A default fills the placeholder when the contact has no value for it, for example {"checkout_url": "https://example.com/checkout"}. The object replaces all saved defaults. An empty object clears them. |
| `confirm_live` | boolean | No |  | Set to true only after the user explicitly confirms the change to a live record. A live record affects real contacts now. Leave it out for drafts. |

## create-sequence-step-tool

**Create Sequence Step Tool**

> Add a draft step to an existing sequence. Steps are always created as drafts. Activate a step with set-sequence-step-status after the user confirms. Set how long after the previous step it sends with delay_type (days or hours) and delay_days. Optionally pass step filters: a contact who does not match them skips this step only. Find the sequence id with list-sequences-tool and a verified sender with view-newsletter-filters-tool. Returns the new step id and status.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sequence_id` | integer | Yes |  | The id of the sequence to add the step to. |
| `delay_type` | string | Yes | `days`, `hours` | Unit for the delay before this step sends: "days" or "hours". |
| `delay_days` | integer | Yes |  | How many days (max 365) or hours (max 8760) after the previous step to send. Use 0 to send immediately on enrollment for the first step. |
| `email_identity_id` | integer | Yes |  | Verified sender identity id to send this step from. |
| `subject` | string | No |  | Email subject line. Supports {{ variable }} template tags. |
| `preview_text` | string | No |  | Inbox preview / preheader text. |
| `html_content` | string | No |  | HTML body of the step. Plain-text is derived automatically. |
| `filters` | array of object | No |  | Step filters. A contact who does not match them skips only this step and moves on to the next step. The sequence filters still apply first. Use view-newsletter-filters-tool to build the array. Omit to send this step to every contact in the sequence. |
| `filters[].connector` | string | No | `and`, `or` | How this filter joins the previous one. Defaults to "and". |
| `filters[].category` | string | No | `attributes`, `tags`, `lists`, `topics`, `date`, `engagement`, `location` | The filter category. |
| `filters[].mode` | string | No | `all`, `any`, `none` | Match mode for attributes/tags/lists/topics (location uses any\|none). |
| `filters[].operator` | string | No |  | Operator for date or engagement filters. |
| `filters[].field` | string | No |  | Field for location filters: country or timezone. |
| `filters[].values` | array | No |  | Filter values. Shape depends on category — see view-newsletter-filters-tool. |

## set-sequence-status

**Set Sequence Status Tool**

> Activate (status "live") or pause (status "draft", or its alias "paused") a sequence. The result returns the stored status: "live" or "draft". A paused sequence has the status "draft". This affects real contacts, so the first call only returns a preview: the change, the enrolled contacts, the pending mails, the live steps and the live automations that add contacts to the sequence. Nothing is saved. Show the preview to the user, and after the user confirms, call the tool again with the same arguments and confirm_live set to true. Never set confirm_live without that confirmation. A sequence sends only through its live steps, so activate the steps with set-sequence-step-status too. The dashboard runs the same checks: activation fails when the account cannot send email. A live step without a {{ unsubscribe_url }} link or a missing postal address never blocks the activation. The preview and the result list them in warnings. Show the warnings to the user. Find sequence ids with list-sequences-tool.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sequence_id` | integer | Yes |  | Id of the sequence. Use list-sequences-tool to discover sequence ids. |
| `status` | string | Yes | `draft`, `live`, `paused` | "live" activates the sequence. "draft" stops it. "paused" is an alias of "draft". |
| `confirm_live` | boolean | No |  | Set to true only after the user explicitly confirms the change to a live record. A live record affects real contacts now. Leave it out for drafts. |

## set-sequence-step-status

**Set Sequence Step Status Tool**

> Activate (status "live") or pause (status "draft", or its alias "paused") one step of a sequence. The result returns the stored statuses: "live" or "draft". A paused step has the status "draft". This affects real contacts, so the first call only returns a preview: the change, the contacts enrolled in the sequence and the pending mails of this step. Nothing is saved. Show the preview to the user, and after the user confirms, call the tool again with the same arguments and confirm_live set to true. Never set confirm_live without that confirmation. The dashboard runs the same checks: activation fails when the account cannot send email or the step has no subject or body. A missing {{ unsubscribe_url }} link or a missing postal address never blocks the activation. The preview and the result list them in warnings. Show the warnings to the user. A live step sends only while its sequence is live. Find step ids with sequence-content-tool.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sequence_step_id` | integer | Yes |  | Id of the sequence step. Use sequence-content-tool to discover step ids. |
| `status` | string | Yes | `draft`, `live`, `paused` | "live" activates the step. "draft" stops it. "paused" is an alias of "draft". |
| `confirm_live` | boolean | No |  | Set to true only after the user explicitly confirms the change to a live record. A live record affects real contacts now. Leave it out for drafts. |

Does not send to the sequence audience and does not start or advance the sequence for anyone. Find the sequence and step ids with list-sequences-tool and sequence-content-tool.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sequence_id` | integer | Yes |  | The id of the sequence the step belongs to. |
| `step_id` | integer | Yes |  | The id of the sequence step to send a test copy of. |

## list-contacts

**List Contacts Tool**

> List the contacts of the authenticated account, oldest id first. Filter with "filters" in the view-newsletter-filters-tool format (tags, lists, topics, attributes, dates, engagement, location) and with "search" on the name or email. Unsubscribed contacts are excluded unless include_unsubscribed is true. Each contact includes its tag names, list ids and custom attributes. To read the next page, send next_after_id from the result as after_id. The cursor stays correct when you change the listed contacts between pages, so use this tool to collect the ids for bulk-update-contacts.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filters` | array of object | No |  | Audience filters in the view-newsletter-filters-tool format. Omit to list every contact. |
| `filters[].connector` | string | No | `and`, `or` | How this filter joins the previous one. Defaults to "and". |
| `filters[].category` | string | No | `attributes`, `tags`, `lists`, `topics`, `date`, `engagement`, `location` | The filter category. |
| `filters[].mode` | string | No | `all`, `any`, `none` | Match mode for attributes/tags/lists/topics (location uses any\|none). |
| `filters[].operator` | string | No |  | Operator for date or engagement filters. |
| `filters[].field` | string | No |  | Field for location filters: country or timezone. |
| `filters[].values` | array | No |  | Filter values. Shape depends on category — see view-newsletter-filters-tool. |
| `search` | string | No |  | Optional case-insensitive search on the contact name or email. |
| `include_unsubscribed` | boolean | No |  | Include unsubscribed contacts. Default false. |
| `after_id` | integer | No |  | Return only contacts with an id above this value. Send next_after_id from the previous page. |
| `per_page` | integer | No |  | Page size (1-100, default 25). |

## create-contact

**Create Contact Tool**

> Create a contact for the authenticated account, or reuse the contact that already has this email. Optional name, tag names, and one list. A new blacklisted email is saved as unsubscribed. An existing email keeps attributes you do not send. Tags are added and never removed — removing a tag is not available through this API. When list_id is set, the contact is added to that list, and a list that requires opt-in queues the opt-in email. The subscription never changes: an unsubscribed contact stays unsubscribed. Find list ids with view-newsletter-filters-tool. Returns the contact id and whether a new row was created.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | Yes |  | Email address. Reuses the account contact with this exact email when one exists. |
| `name` | string | No |  | Optional display name. Omitted leaves the current name unchanged. |
| `tags` | array of string | No |  | Optional tag names to add. Unknown names are created. Existing tags on the contact are kept. To remove tags, use bulk-update-contacts. |
| `list_id` | integer | No |  | Optional mailing list id. Find ids with view-newsletter-filters-tool. A list that requires opt-in queues the opt-in email. |

## add-contact-to-list

**Add Contact To List Tool**

> Add an existing contact to a mailing list without removing their other lists. A list that requires opt-in queues the opt-in email and does not mark the contact opted in. The subscription never changes: an unsubscribed contact stays unsubscribed. Calling it again for a list they already belong to does not send another subscription event. To change many contacts at once, use bulk-update-contacts. Find the contact with find-contact and the list id with view-newsletter-filters-tool.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `contact_id` | integer | Yes |  | Id of the contact. Find it with find-contact. |
| `list_id` | integer | Yes |  | Id of the mailing list. Find it with view-newsletter-filters-tool. |

## add-tags-to-contact

**Add Tags To Contact Tool**

> Add tags to an existing contact by name. Tags already on the contact stay. A name that does not exist yet is created for this account. create-tag-tool remains the strict way to create a tag and still errors on a duplicate name. To remove tags, or to change many contacts at once, use bulk-update-contacts. Find the contact with find-contact.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `contact_id` | integer | Yes |  | Id of the contact. Find it with find-contact. |
| `tags` | array of string | Yes |  | Tag names to add. Unknown names are created. Existing tags on the contact are kept. To remove tags, use bulk-update-contacts. |

## remove-contact-from-list

**Remove Contact From List Tool**

> Remove a contact from one mailing list. Their other lists stay. The contact row is not deleted. The removal runs the live list automations of the account. Find the contact with find-contact and the list id with view-newsletter-filters-tool.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `contact_id` | integer | Yes |  | Id of the contact. Find it with find-contact. |
| `list_id` | integer | Yes |  | Id of the mailing list to remove them from. |

## bulk-update-contacts

**Bulk Update Contacts Tool**

> Update up to 100 existing contacts in one call. Each item names one contact by contact_id or by exact email, and gives its own changes: name, add_tags, remove_tags, set_attributes, remove_attributes, add_to_lists and remove_from_lists. Only the fields you send change. Unknown tag names in add_tags are created. Unknown tag names in remove_tags are ignored. set_attributes merges into the custom attributes of the contact. Adding a contact to a list that requires opt-in queues the opt-in email. Adding a contact to a list never changes the subscription. Tag, list and attribute changes run the live automations of the account. Items are independent: a failed item does not stop the other items, and the result reports each item as updated or failed. Find the contacts with list-contacts and the list ids with view-newsletter-filters-tool.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `contacts` | array of object | Yes |  | The contacts to update (1-100). Each item has its own changes. |
| `contacts[].contact_id` | integer | No |  | Id of the contact. Send contact_id or email. |
| `contacts[].email` | string | No |  | Exact email of the contact. Used only when contact_id is not sent. |
| `contacts[].name` | string | No |  | New display name. Send null to clear it. |
| `contacts[].add_tags` | array of string | No |  | Tag names to add. Unknown names are created. Existing tags stay. |
| `contacts[].remove_tags` | array of string | No |  | Tag names to remove. Unknown names are ignored. |
| `contacts[].set_attributes` | object | No |  | Custom attributes to set, as {"name": value}. A value is a string (maximum 255 characters), a number or a boolean. Attributes that you do not send stay. The names "name" and "email" are reserved. |
| `contacts[].remove_attributes` | array of string | No |  | Custom attribute names to remove from the contact. |
| `contacts[].add_to_lists` | array of integer | No |  | List ids to add the contact to. A list that requires opt-in queues the opt-in email. |
| `contacts[].remove_from_lists` | array of integer | No |  | List ids to remove the contact from. |

Use the returned id with email-identity-details-tool, refresh-email-identity-status-tool or update-email-identity-tracking-tool. Only identities with identity_status "verified" can send mail.

## email-identity-details-tool

**Email Identity Details Tool**

> Show a single sender identity in full: verification status, MAIL FROM subdomain, AWS region, custom link domain, tracking flags and the DNS records (DKIM CNAMEs, MAIL FROM MX/TXT and DMARC TXT) the domain owner must publish, each with a verified flag. Use it to guide someone through DNS setup. Find the id with list-email-identities-tool.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email_identity_id` | integer | Yes |  | The id of the sender identity. |

## create-email-identity-tool

**Create Email Identity Tool**

> Create a sender identity for the authenticated account. Registers the email's domain in the account's own AWS SES, sets up a MAIL FROM subdomain (default "mas.<domain>") and a per-identity configuration set, and returns the DNS records the domain owner must publish before the identity can verify. The account must already have AWS credentials configured in the dashboard. Set existing_aws_identity to true to import a domain that is already verified in SES instead of creating it. After the DNS records are published, call refresh-email-identity-status-tool to check verification.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | Yes |  | Sender email address, for example "hello@example.com". Its domain is registered in SES. |
| `name` | string | No |  | Optional display name for the sender. |
| `existing_aws_identity` | boolean | No |  | Set to true when the domain is already registered in the account's SES and should be imported instead of created. Defaults to false. |
| `open_tracking_enabled` | boolean | No |  | Track opens for mail sent from this identity. Defaults to true. |
| `click_tracking_enabled` | boolean | No |  | Track clicks for mail sent from this identity. Defaults to true. |
| `mail_from_subdomain` | string | No |  | Optional custom MAIL FROM subdomain, lowercase, for example "bounce.example.com". Defaults to "mas.<domain>". |

## view-automation-options

**View Automation Options Tool**

> Describe the building blocks of an automation for the authenticated account: the trigger condition types, the action types, and the lists, tags, sequences, contact attributes and link names that a condition or action can reference by id or name. Use the result to assemble the "condition" and "actions" for create-automation and update-automation. A paused automation can use a draft sequence in an "add_sequence" action. The automation can go live only when that sequence is live.

This tool takes no arguments.

## create-automation

**Create Automation Tool**

> Create an automation for the authenticated account: when the trigger condition happens to a contact, the actions run on that contact. Automations are always created paused (is_live false). A paused automation can add contacts to a draft sequence. Switch it on with set-automation-status after its sequences are live. Call view-automation-options first to find the condition types, action types and the list, tag and sequence ids. Returns the new automation.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes |  | Name for the automation. |
| `type` | string | No | `simple` | Automation type. The only type is "simple". |
| `condition` | object | Yes |  | The trigger. Use view-automation-options to find the ids. |
| `condition.type` | string | No | `contact_added_to_list`, `removed_from_list`, `tag_added`, `removed_tag`, `added_to_sequence`, `sequence_finished`, `attribute_changed`, `link_clicked` | The event that starts the automation. |
| `condition.value` | string | No |  | The list, tag or sequence id of the event. For "attribute_changed" with operator "changed_to", the new attribute value. For "link_clicked", the link name. |
| `condition.attribute` | string | No |  | Only for "attribute_changed": the contact attribute name. |
| `condition.operator` | string | No | `changed_to`, `changed` | Only for "attribute_changed": "changed_to" needs a value, "changed" matches any change. |
| `actions` | array of object | Yes |  | What happens to the contact, in order. |
| `actions[].type` | string | No | `add_tag`, `add_list`, `remove_tag`, `remove_list`, `add_sequence` | What to do with the contact. |
| `actions[].value` | integer | No |  | The tag, list or sequence id. A paused automation can add contacts to a draft sequence. The sequence must be live before the automation goes live. |

## update-automation

**Update Automation Tool**

> Update an automation of the authenticated account. A live automation (is_live true) runs on contacts now, so the tool refuses the change until you ask the user to confirm and call it again with confirm_live set to true. Paused automations need no confirmation. The live flag never changes here: use set-automation-status. A paused automation can point an "add_sequence" action to a draft sequence. A live automation needs live sequences. Only the fields you pass are changed: a passed condition replaces the whole condition and a passed actions array replaces all actions. Use view-automation-options for the ids. Returns the updated automation.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `automation_id` | integer | Yes |  | Id of the automation to update. Use list-automations to discover ids. |
| `name` | string | No |  | Name for the automation. |
| `type` | string | No | `simple` | Automation type. The only type is "simple". |
| `condition` | object | No |  | The trigger. Use view-automation-options to find the ids. |
| `condition.type` | string | No | `contact_added_to_list`, `removed_from_list`, `tag_added`, `removed_tag`, `added_to_sequence`, `sequence_finished`, `attribute_changed`, `link_clicked` | The event that starts the automation. |
| `condition.value` | string | No |  | The list, tag or sequence id of the event. For "attribute_changed" with operator "changed_to", the new attribute value. For "link_clicked", the link name. |
| `condition.attribute` | string | No |  | Only for "attribute_changed": the contact attribute name. |
| `condition.operator` | string | No | `changed_to`, `changed` | Only for "attribute_changed": "changed_to" needs a value, "changed" matches any change. |
| `actions` | array of object | No |  | What happens to the contact, in order. |
| `actions[].type` | string | No | `add_tag`, `add_list`, `remove_tag`, `remove_list`, `add_sequence` | What to do with the contact. |
| `actions[].value` | integer | No |  | The tag, list or sequence id. A paused automation can add contacts to a draft sequence. The sequence must be live before the automation goes live. |
| `confirm_live` | boolean | No |  | Set to true only after the user explicitly confirms the change to a live record. A live record affects real contacts now. Leave it out for drafts. |

## set-automation-status

**Set Automation Status Tool**

> Switch an automation on (is_live true) or off (is_live false). This affects real contacts, so the first call only returns a preview: the change, the condition, the actions and the sequences the automation adds contacts to. Nothing is saved. Show the preview to the user, and after the user confirms, call the tool again with the same arguments and confirm_live set to true. Never set confirm_live without that confirmation. A live automation runs on matching events from now on. It does not run on contacts that matched before. The dashboard runs the same check: an automation with an "add_sequence" action can go live only when that sequence is live, because a live automation drops contacts it cannot enroll. Find automation ids with list-automations.

| Argument | Type | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `automation_id` | integer | Yes |  | Id of the automation. Use list-automations to discover ids. |
| `is_live` | boolean | Yes |  | true switches the automation on. false pauses it. |
| `confirm_live` | boolean | No |  | Set to true only after the user explicitly confirms the change to a live record. A live record affects real contacts now. Leave it out for drafts. |
